study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
exposure: Prolonged latent phase (defined as <6 cm dilated after >=12 h with ruptured membranes and oxytocin)
outcome: Cesarean delivery (CD) after reaching active phase
cohort: Participants were term, singleton gestations with intact membranes and unfavorable cervix undergoing induction of labor at two large academic hospitals, who subsequently reached active labor.
finding: Among term patients undergoing induction, a prolonged latent phase is associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery and composite maternal and neonatal morbidities after reaching active labor, particularly in nulliparous patients.
mod_finding: Among patients with a vaginal delivery, a prolonged latent phase was associated with higher maternal morbidity; however, patients who underwent CD had the highest risk of morbidity, regardless of latent phase duration.
